einzeiler: Oscar nominee Josh Fox discusses climate refugees, his new film, and finding community.
kurzfassung: Filmmaker Josh Fox discusses his new HBO documentary, The Welcome Table, which explores the global crisis of climate refugees. He examines the political and ecological roots of mass displacement, drawing parallels between natural disasters and systematic oppression. Fox also reflects on the role of art, music, and mutual aid in building resilience against future crises.
stichpunkte: Josh Fox directed the documentary The Welcome Table, focusing on climate refugees across six continents.
The project was inspired by an unfinished book by James Baldwin and a song by jazz artist John Boutte.
The film highlights climate disasters in the United States, including wildfires in Paradise and Boulder.
Fox draws attention to the toxic aftermath of natural disasters and the severe risks of water contamination.
Current international law does not recognize climate change as a valid category for refugee status.
New Orleans serves as the emotional and musical backbone of the film, celebrating resilience through culture.
Fox critiques the massive energy and water demands of data centers and AI development.
The documentary avoids traditional talking heads, relying instead on personal stories from people on the front lines.

kapitel.titel: Music and Resilience in New Orleans
Data Centers and the New Climate Battle
Systematic Displacement and the IPCC Report

clips.hook: What is the opposite of a wall?
clips.text: The director explains that physical border barriers serve primarily as hostile symbols rather than effective deterrents, prompting the search for a metaphorical alternative.

clips.hook: Climate change is not a category for refugees
clips.text: Existing international legal frameworks protect individuals fleeing political or religious persecution, but completely fail to shelter those displaced by environmental collapse.

clips.hook: Millions of tons of earth coming at your neighborhood
clips.text: Atmospheric changes fuel torrential downpours that trigger massive mountain landslides, wiping out entire residential blocks in seconds.

clips.hook: The only time emissions dropped was during COVID
clips.text: Global lockdowns during the initial months of the pandemic proved that drastic societal pauses are the only proven method for significantly reducing carbon output.

clips.hook: Nobody wants to leave their home
clips.text: Displaced populations do not migrate out of ambition or desire, but are forced to flee when environmental conditions completely destroy their means of survival.

beschreibung:
Josh Fox is an independent filmmaker, playwright, and environmental activist best known for his Oscar-nominated and Emmy-winning 2010 documentary, GASLAND. He is also the founder and artistic director of International WOW Company, a film and theater company working closely with actors, filmmakers, theater-makers, writers, activists, and artists from diverse cultural backgrounds, including activist communities in sustainable energy and design, creating work that addresses current national and global environmental, social and political crises. As a filmmaker, Fox’s work has been featured on HBO, Netflix, and premiered at both the Sundance and Tribeca Film Festivals. His debut documentary film, GASLAND, earned a Special Jury Prize at Sundance as well as an Oscar nomination and Emmy win. As a theatrical director, he has been praised by the New York Times as "one of the most adventurous impresarios of the New York avant-garde”. Fox has also contributed as a journalist to publications such as Rolling Stone, The Daily Beast, NowThis, AJ+ and Huffington Post. Fox’s documentary work returns to HBO this summer 2026 with his latest film, THE WELCOME TABLE, which tells the story of climate refugees across six continents who were displaced from their homes by climate disasters.
